sentences.text: . The petitioner had approached before the learned Court below praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 06.05.2023 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.
The prosecution case in short is that, the informant/victim lodged a written report alleging therein that she had in love relationship with the petitioner since long.
On the relevant day, the petitioner took her and had court marriage with her and stayed as husband and wife.
After some days, the petitioner abused her in filthy languages and tortured her both physically and mentally for dowry.
It is alleged that the petitioner had also assaulted her and drove her out from his house.

Hence, the F.I.R.

sentences.text: From the evidence collected by the police form part of the charge-sheet, it reveals that the victim had in relationship with the petitioner since the year 2010.
At that point in time, the victim was a minor girl.
Eventually in the year 2019, they married and stayed as husband and wife till 2024.

Due to misunderstanding cropped in their marriage, the victim has filed the F.I.R. alleging the offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(3)/498-A/506/313 of I.P.C. read with Section 4(2)/6 of the POCSO Act against the petitioner .

After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed on 04.07.2024 for alleged offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(3)/498-A/506 of the I.P.C. read with Section 4/6 of the POCSO Act.
6.
Pursuant to the order 28.05.2024 passed by the coordinate Bench of this Court, the informant/victim along with her counsel has appeared through Virtual Mode.
The victim opposed the bail and submits that once the petitioner is released on bail, he may threaten her.
7. I have given a careful consideration to the facts of the present case and perused the evidence on record.
It reveals from the record that the petitioner and the victim had been in relationship since 2010 and eventually they married in the year 2019.
The marriage had gone wrong due to the misunderstanding.
Hence, the F.I.R. has been lodged.

The petitioner is in custody since 03.05.2024.
8.
Regard being had to the period of custody from 03.05.2024 and the nature of accusation, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:-
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on each date of hearing without fail.
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.

To alley the apprehension of the victim that she may be threatened by the petitioner, additional conditions shall also be imposed by the Court below while releasing the petitioner on bail to ensure that the petitioner in no manner shall harm the victim or threaten her.
9. At the same time, I am of the considered view that the Court below shall make an endeavor to settle the dispute between the parties by referring the matter to DLSA for mediation.

In the event, the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
10. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
